page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard1.1 is an entry-level compute instance belonging to the first-generation Standard shape family. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture and operates on an Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The virtualization layer assigns 1 dedicated physical core, resulting in 2 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading, paired with 7.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.5 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The VM.Standard1.1 shape does not include local disk storage, meaning persistent storage and operating system images must be managed using attached network block volumes. Hardware acceleration is not present on this shape, with zero physical GPUs allocated. Network configuration includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

With its modest resource footprint, the instance is positioned as an economical baseline option for low-intensity cloud tasks. Because it relies on an older Intel Xeon microarchitecture and dual vCPU threading, it is constrained for heavy computational throughput but functions effectively for utility-oriented duties. Best-fit deployments include lightweight web serving, development and test sandboxes, low-traffic microservices, and auxiliary monitoring services.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard1.1 is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the Standard shape series. Powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the configuration includes 1 dedicated physical core, 2 vCPUs, and 7.0 GB of system memory. The shape provides no local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring external block storage for data persistence and operating system installations. It contains no GPU accelerators but includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. Offering a balanced allocation of memory per vCPU, VM.Standard1.1 serves general computing demands that do not require intense processing power or high storage throughput. The instance profile is suited for low-traffic web applications, staging environments, basic development testing, and lightweight background automation tasks.
